newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Geneva private bank cuts cash exposure.
newsitem.headline: Geneva private bank cuts cash exposure.

text.p: Swiss private bank Union Bancaire Privee said on Monday it had cut its cash exposure in favour of alternative investments while keeping its equities portfolio overweight in European shares.

Following a strategy meeting, it said cash holdings were cut to 25 percent from 30 and alternative investments raised to 20 from 15 in its balanced dollar portfolio. The share of bonds and shares was unchanged at 30 and 25 percent respectively.

The Geneva-based bank said its investment committee recommended overweighting European financial assets, including selected equities in France, Germany, Switzerland and the Netherlands but cutting exposure to Finland and Britain.

The bank's overall equities portfolio was underweight in the Asian Pacific region. Assets allocated in Asia favoured Hong Kong, Singapore and Thailand and were underweight in Malaysia, Australia, South Korea and Japan.
Shares in Hong Kong make up about four percent of the bank's stock portfolio. --- Reuters Geneva Newsroom 41-22 733 38 31
